rationale: The residual errors are all typing confusions driven by recur_frac>=0.9, which fires for reverse (reversed footage), room_swap (returning/static scene), and loop alike, plus dup_dense firing on static swaps and high echo firing on room_swap. I reframed recur_frac/dup_dense as corruption evidence only, made the typing guide ordered so a confirmed location change beats both echo and recur_frac, and noted reverse's echo override. I also stressed that splices leave no free-signal trace and that loop requires the same scene as its source, pushing the model to judge near recurrence boundaries before typing none or loop.

pack.task: Decide whether this 30s video clip was edited, and which candidate boundaries (if any) need a VLM continuity check.
pack.conclude_crit: stop gathering evidence and report the final verdict
pack.judge_crit_template: run the VLM continuity check on candidate {i} at frame {frame} (~{secs:.1f}s)

signals.recur_frac_max: fraction of frames that are near-exact replays of an earlier frame (lag 2-10s). >=0.9 means the clip is EDITED, but is NOT specific to loop: reverse (reversed footage) and room_swap (original scene returning, or a static still swapped in) also replay frames and reach ~1.0. Use recur_frac for corruption only, then apply the typing disambiguators. 0.5-0.8 is ambiguous (same-scene splices reach ~0.6).
signals.dup_dense_last_frame: last frame of a dense run of adjacent-duplicate frames. Fires on setpts slowdown (timewarp) OR on a static swapped-in segment (room_swap). Non-null alone does not prove timewarp: if a scene change (photo_jump/scenecut) sits at the run boundary, suspect room_swap; null on clean/other.
signals.echo_best_score: self-anchored 4-factor score: high only when TWO discontinuities echo (content after seam A matches content after seam B). >10 indicates reverse, but note reversed footage also replays frames so reverse ALSO shows recur_frac~1.0; a matched pair does not by itself beat a confirmed location change. Magnitude beyond >10 adds nothing and values >>1e4 can be degenerate. best_pair is always the argmax, so a pair scoring <10 is NOT an echo. Two discontinuities WITHOUT high echo => room_swap or splice, not reverse.
signals.scenecut_iframe_frames: frames where the encoder inserted a scene-cut I-frame; flags abrupt visual discontinuity. BASE RATE: clean clips average ~2-3 per 30s from natural motion. A room_swap places cuts at BOTH its swap-in and swap-out boundaries; a loop usually shows one seam.
signals.photo_jump_top3: top frame-difference peaks. z is normalized WITHIN the clip, so the largest peak always scores high even on clean clips — read peak POSITIONS and co-occurrence, not z magnitude. TWO strong peaks a few seconds apart that flank repeated content suggest room_swap's two boundaries.

pack.typing_guide: Type by arrangement, not recur_frac alone (many edit types replay frames): 1) a judge-confirmed change to a DIFFERENT place/location, or scene-cut/photo_jump peaks at TWO boundaries with a different scene between them => room_swap. 2) else echo_best_score>10 with same-scene mirror content => reverse (reversed footage also replays, so this overrides loop). 3) else recur_frac>=0.9 with ONE seam and no scene change => loop (loop must be the SAME scene as its source — never call loop when a different place appears). 4) else dup_dense_last_frame with no coincident scene change => timewarp. 5) else ONE confirmed discontinuity with the SAME scene on both sides => splice (even if break_kind says scene_change). 6) no discontinuities and quiet signals that survive candidate checks => none.
pack.candidate_note: Each candidate is a suspicious transition the gates flagged. BASE RATE: the gates are permissive and nominate ~4-8 candidates per clip INCLUDING on clean clips, so a candidate existing is weak evidence — only its VLM verdict is strong. A VLM check costs ~2s and is near-perfect precision. splices leave NO free-signal trace, so quiet signals do not rule them out. recur_frac>=0.9 does NOT distinguish loop from reverse or room_swap — judge at least one candidate near each recurrence boundary before typing. Before concluding 'none', check the strongest photo_jump/scenecut candidates unless a decisive free signal (echo>10 or dup_dense) already explains the clip.

questions.action: What is the best next step?
questions.corrupted: This clip contains an artificial temporal discontinuity (an edit: replayed footage, reversed segment, swapped scene, cut/splice, or retimed segment).
questions.break_type: Which edit type best fits the evidence?
questions.sufficient: The current evidence is sufficient to conclude with confidence; more VLM checks would not change the verdict.
questions.is_type_template: The evidence indicates this clip was edited with a {type} corruption ({desc}).

type_desc.loop: footage of the SAME scene repeats — a segment is replayed
type_desc.reverse: a segment plays backward in time
type_desc.room_swap: the scene/location changes to a different place then returns to the original
type_desc.splice: a hard cut joins non-contiguous footage of the same scene
type_desc.timewarp: part of the clip plays at altered speed (slowed or sped up)
